g.text: Now scripted (green solid) — built and tested live this session (2026-09-04)
Still manual (gray dashed) — judgment work that stays a human/Claude job on purpose
Partially scripted (orange) — the judgment core stays manual, mechanical parts around it are scripted
Safety / verification pattern — stage 10, a per-task judgment call on whether to bother
Scripts added this session (all in scripts/ci/ unless noted, all committed + pushed):
start_task.sh — creates the per-task worktree (was: 1 manual git command, low risk but still retyped every time)
dispatch_cline.sh — cycles the 4-model free-worker fallback chain automatically on "hook dispatch failed" (verified 4/4 hit rate
against every real provider failure this session: a rate limit, a provider overload, a delisted model, an idle timeout)
stress_gate.sh [N] — re-runs the full test gate N times, stops on first failure (was: a hand-typed for-loop, retyped 5+ times)
land_task.sh — the full stash → merge → 3x gate → push → worktree cleanup → WIP-restore sequence in one call; refuses to
guess on a merge conflict or a post-merge gate failure — reports clearly and stops instead (was: ~8 manual steps, fumbled twice by hand)
scripts/dev/keep_awake.sh — prevents display sleep/screensaver-lock during a manual playtest session (synthetic game input
doesn't count as real user activity to macOS — hit a real lock screen mid-session before this existed)
What stayed manual on purpose: writing the dispatch prompt itself, reading the actual diff, judging correctness, writing commit/merge messages,
and deciding when the free-worker-consult (stage 10) gate is worth the extra dispatch. Automation removed identical-every-time scaffolding, not judgment.
Note: stage 9 (Draw Things) is fired by n8n independently of the 1→6 task loop — its arrow originates from stage 8, not from any stage on the left.
